title: Dirichlet-Guided Group Forecasting for Alleviating Over-smoothing in Time Series Forecasting
claim: Averaging multiple plausible futures yields a weakened, over-smoothed forecast; inferring latent modes first preserves distinct trajectories.
layout: 3 columns, left-to-right; problem and fix plots, artifact examples at right
description: A three-column figure with numbered headers. Panel 1 (red theme) plots temperature history in black. At the forecast start, blue upward, green stable and orange downward futures fan out, and a thick red averaged forecast runs flat through the middle. A pink box below shows many futures collapsing into one trajectory. Panel 2 (blue theme) uses the same history. A latent mode inference box feeds three nodes, z1, z2 and z3, which give three separate colored forecasts. A blue box below shows the modes preserved. Panel 3 stacks three small plots: direction erased, oscillation attenuated and spike-time averaging. Each plot shows colored plausible futures against a red smoothed result. Sun, cloud and rain icons mark the modes. A shared legend runs along the bottom. The eye goes first to the diverging colored curves and the red average line.
caption: Illustration of over-smoothing and mode-preserving forecasting. Under the same observed history, multiple latent dynamical modes may lead to distinct plausible futures. A centralized forecast can compress these incompatible modes into an averaged trajectory with weakened dynamics, whereas mode-preserving forecasting maintains separate mode-conditioned trajectories.
abstract: Time series forecasting often suffers from over-smoothing, especially when future dynamics are multi-modal. Forecasts may follow the coarse trend of the observed future, but fail to preserve sharp changes, oscillations, turning points, and regime transitions that define plausible dynamic evolution. In this work, we revisit over-smoothing from the perspective of latent dynamical mode compression: under partial observation and single-realization supervision, multiple plausible future modes can be weakened, merged, or averaged during forecasting. Based on this view, we propose Dirichlet-Guided Group Forecasting (DGF), a mode-preserving forecasting framework that explicitly models multiple mode-conditioned predictive distributions and uncertainty over their selection probabilities. DGF uses a Dirichlet-guided hierarchical sampling mechanism and reward-based optimization to encourage forecasts that are accurate, dynamically consistent, and mode-distinct. Extensive experiments on real-world forecasting benchmarks show that DGF reduces over-smoothing while improving forecasting accuracy, diversity, and dynamical consistency. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/Zh-XY22/DGF
